newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Russia sees foreign investment rising to $20 bln.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees foreign investment rising to $20 bln.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said he was sure foreign investment in his country would reach $20 billion by the year 2000.
He told a news conference at the World Economic Forum that foreign investors would move in as a reshaping of Russian laws gave them more confidence of legal protection.
"We are setting up the structures they want to see," he said. "This will give them more confidence."
Chernomyrdin said that in 1995 foreign investment in Russia totalled only $2 billion and last year it was $6 billion.
"I am sure, I am certain, that by the year 2000 it will reach $20 billion," he added. "There are still problems but we will overcome them."
Russia would never return to its communist past. "There can be no going back for us under any circumstances," he declared.
"Russia will not swerve from the path of democratic reform and of creating a strong market economy." ((Robert Evans, Davos Newsroom 41-81 413 14 49))
